knowledge-base.overview: Blazor (.NET 8+) guardrails, component lifecycle, hosting models, state management, JavaScript interop, and testing. Applies to WebAssembly, Server, and Blazor United (per-component render modes) apps. Loaded automatically when agents work on .razor files or Blazor .cs component code-behind files.

core-principles.principle: Build encapsulated .razor components that own their state and rendering. One responsibility per component.
Choose WebAssembly, Server, or Blazor United (hybrid SSR + interactive) per component in .NET 8.
Share models, validation logic, and domain types between client and server via a Shared project.
Leverage C# nullable reference types and strongly-typed component parameters.
Understand when each lifecycle method runs to avoid memory leaks and race conditions.

row.best-for: Offline-capable apps, PWAs, reduced server load
Low latency, SEO, thin clients, real-time apps
Per-component render mode selection, maximum flexibility

guardrail.rule: Never call JavaScript interop (IJSRuntime) in OnInitialized or OnInitializedAsync. The DOM is not ready at that point. Use OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender) instead.
Never mutate [Parameter] properties directly inside the component that receives them. Use local state initialized from parameters in OnParametersSet.
Implement IDisposable (or IAsyncDisposable) on any component that subscribes to events, creates timers, or registers state change callbacks. Unsubscribe in Dispose().
Use EventCallback<T> for parent-child communication in component parameters. Never use Action<T> — EventCallback automatically calls StateHasChanged on the correct component.
guardrail.bad: [Parameter] public Action<long> OnEdit { get; set; } = null!; // Action won't trigger parent re-render

guardrail.rule: Use [Parameter, EditorRequired] for required parameters to get compile-time warnings when callers omit them.
Use @key directive on list-rendered items so Blazor's DOM diffing can match elements to model instances correctly.
Use <Virtualize> for large collections. Never @foreach over more than ~50 items in a render-intensive loop without virtualization.
Validate all inputs server-side. Client-side EditForm validation with DataAnnotationsValidator is for UX only — enforce on the API.
Wrap component trees with <ErrorBoundary> to prevent one failing component from crashing the entire page.
Call StateHasChanged() only when necessary. Excessive calls cause performance degradation. Blazor re-renders automatically after event handlers.
Use CascadingValue for widely shared, infrequently changing state (theme, auth). Avoid CascadingValue for frequently updating data — it triggers full subtree re-renders.

project-structure.description: Three-project layout: Client (Blazor UI), Server (API), Shared (models + DTOs).
project-structure.example: MyApp/ ├── MyApp.Client/ # Blazor WebAssembly / interactive components │ ├── Pages/ # Routable components (@page directive) │ │ ├── Home.razor │ │ └── Users/ │ │ ├── UserList.razor │ │ ├── UserDetail.razor │ │ └── UserForm.razor │ ├── Components/ # Reusable non-routable components │ │ ├── Layout/ │ │ │ ├── MainLayout.razor │ │ │ └── NavMenu.razor │ │ └── Common/ │ │ ├── LoadingSpinner.razor │ │ └── Modal.razor │ ├── Services/ # Client-side typed HttpClient services │ │ ├── IUserService.cs │ │ └── UserService.cs │ ├── State/ # Observable state services │ │ └── AppState.cs │ ├── _Imports.razor # Global @using directives │ ├── App.razor # Root component + Router │ └── Program.cs # DI, HttpClient base address ├── MyApp.Server/ # ASP.NET Core API host │ ├── Controllers/ or Endpoints/ │ └── Program.cs ├── MyApp.Shared/ # Shared across Client and Server │ ├── Models/ # Domain models with DataAnnotations │ └── DTOs/ # Request/response records ├── tests/ │ ├── MyApp.Client.Tests/ # bUnit component tests │ └── MyApp.Server.Tests/ # API integration tests └── MyApp.sln

pattern.name: Page Component with Data Loading
pattern.description: Routable page with loading/error/empty state handling.

pattern.name: Reusable Component with Required Parameters
pattern.description: Component using [Parameter, EditorRequired], EventCallback, and @key-friendly id.
pattern.example:
@User.FirstName @User.LastName
@User.Email @(User.Active ? "Active" : "Inactive")
@code { [Parameter, EditorRequired] public UserResponse User { get; set; } = default!; [Parameter] public EventCallback OnEdit { get; set; } [Parameter] public EventCallback OnDelete { get; set; } }

forms.description: EditForm with DataAnnotationsValidator for client-side UX. Always validate on server too.
forms.example: @code { private CreateUserRequest model = new(); private bool submitting; private async Task HandleSubmit() { submitting = true; try { await UserService.CreateAsync(model); Navigation.NavigateTo("/users"); } finally { submitting = false; } } }

pattern.name: Observable State Service
pattern.description: Singleton state service with OnChange event. Components subscribe and call StateHasChanged.

dotnet8-render-modes.description: Blazor United .NET 8 supports per-component render mode selection.
dotnet8-render-modes.example:
@* Static SSR (default — no interactivity, fastest) *@ <StaticComponent />
@* Interactive Server (SignalR — good for real-time) *@ <InteractiveComponent @rendermode="InteractiveServer" />
@* Interactive WebAssembly (offline-capable after download) *@ <InteractiveComponent @rendermode="InteractiveWebAssembly" />
@* Interactive Auto (starts as Server, switches to WASM when downloaded) *@ <InteractiveComponent @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
@* Streaming — add to pages with slow async data; renders placeholder then streams updates *@ @attribute [StreamRendering]

testing.stack: bUnit, xUnit, Moq or NSubstitute, FluentAssertions

rules.rule: Use bUnit TestContext for isolated component rendering
Use RenderComponent with parameter builders to pass typed parameters
Simulate events with .Click(), .Input(), .Change() on found elements
Verify EventCallback invocation by capturing a flag in a local lambda

quick-reference.item: Use [Parameter, EditorRequired] for required inputs; EventCallback not Action for events
OnInitializedAsync for data loading; OnParametersSet for reacting to param changes; OnAfterRenderAsync for JS interop
IDisposable always when subscribing to events, timers, or state changes
@key on every list item; Virtualize for collections over ~50 items
Observable state service with OnChange event for cross-component state
EditForm + DataAnnotationsValidator for UX; enforce validation server-side too
Only in OnAfterRenderAsync(firstRender); encapsulate behind a service class
.NET 8 United: InteractiveServer / InteractiveWebAssembly / InteractiveAuto per component; StreamRendering for slow async pages
bUnit TestContext; RenderComponent with typed parameter builders; assert markup + event callbacks
